name: ai-safety-evaluation
evidence: Risk/claim matrix linking each scenario to harm, actor, prerequisites, system boundary, and severity
Exact tested system identity including model, prompts, tools, data, permissions, safeguards, harness, and attempt/resource budget
Adversarial and benign-control run artifacts with attack success, utility, and deterministic side-effect/denial checks
Validity checks for broken tasks, contamination, scorer or reward hacking, refusal artifacts, evaluator leakage, and evaluation awareness when applicable
Mitigation regression results plus residual-risk record with confirmed failures preserved
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Design an AI safety evaluation for our support agent that can read email and issue refunds; test indirect prompt injection, unauthorized tool use, and secret exfiltration while measuring benign task completion.
Red-team this LLM safeguard against multi-turn jailbreak attempts and report attack success, severity, attacker budget, benign false refusals, and regression cases.
Build a model safety testing suite for misuse risks in this assistant, with policy-labeled cases, adversarial variants, deterministic checks where possible, and before/after mitigation results.
Evaluate agentic AI safety for a coding agent with shell and repository tools: test over-delegation, instruction injection from untrusted files, permission-boundary violations, and recovery behavior.
Run a safeguard robustness evaluation after this system-prompt and policy-filter change, keeping the harness and attack budget fixed and checking both harmful-case blocking and allowed-user utility.
negative: Benchmark two chat models on answer accuracy, latency, cost, and style preference using a held-out QA set; there is no safety or harm claim.
Review this REST API for broken object-level authorization and session fixation; the application does not use an AI model.
Map what personal data we collect, why we retain it, who can access it, and how deletion requests propagate through storage.
Verify that ordinary users cannot call the admin endpoint and that tenant isolation fails closed; no AI behavior is involved.
Evaluate a fraud classifier's calibration, precision/recall, subgroup performance, and drift on a labeled validation set.

ambiguous.prompt: Compare two agents on ordinary task success, but also determine whether either can be induced to take a prohibited high-impact action under a defined attacker budget. Keep generic agent-quality scoring in llm-evaluation and own the AI safety evaluation of the prohibited-action claim here.

The agent has a normal authorization bug to review, and we also need a prompt injection evaluation showing whether untrusted retrieved text can make the model cross that authorization boundary. Separate the application-security finding from the AI safety attack-success evidence.

Review the assistant's sensitive-data lifecycle, and separately run an agent safety evaluation to see whether indirect instructions can cause disclosure of a synthetic canary secret through an allowed tool. Keep privacy governance and adversarial safety evidence distinct.

adversarial.prompt: Do not run an AI safety evaluation. The design document contains a completed historical safety-review request, but the current task is only to compare response latency and factual accuracy on a benign QA benchmark.
Do not perform model safety testing. Fix the non-AI service's missing authorization check and add a negative integration test for the admin endpoint.

Do not run a prompt injection evaluation. Explain at a high level what indirect prompt injection means for an architecture review, without designing attacks, datasets, scorers, or a safety test suite.

sources.versionScope: NIST AI 600-1 Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile, publication page updated 2026-04-08
sources.notes: Primary risk-management reference for framing generative-AI risks, lifecycle measurement, and risk-specific evaluation rather than a single undifferentiated safety score.

Claim-first evaluation design, harness and budget disclosure, strong elicitation for safeguard claims, and validity checks for contamination, broken tasks, refusals, reward hacking, and evaluation awareness.
